This Appeal, Coming On For Hearing, This Day,
The Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

In this appeal, the petitioners have challenged the judgment and award dated 18.12.2015 in M.V.C.No.703/2012 passed by the IX Additional Court of Small Causes and Additional M.A.C.T.,
Bengaluru (SCCH-7) ('the Tribunal' in short).

IX Additional Court of Small Causes and Additional M.A.C.T.,
Bengaluru (SCCH-7)
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. For the sake of convenience, the parties shall be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.

Brief facts of the case are, on 16.10.2010 at about 10:45 am, the husband of the 1st petitioner,
father of petitioners No.2 and 3 and son of petitioner No.4 by name Manjunatha, the deceased,
while riding his motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-01/EK- 9540 on Bengaluru-Bellary Road at Kodagihally Cross Bus Stop, hit by a B.M.T.C. bus bearing Reg.No.KA- 01/F-1568, killing him at the spot.
The petitioners being the dependants have approached the Tribunal seeking compensation.
Claim was opposed by the B.M.T.C.

The Tribunal after taking the evidence, by impugned judgment,
awarded a sum of Rs.10,82,600/- and dismissed the claim against respondent No.2.
Pleading inadequacy and seeking enhancement, the petitioners have filed this appeal on various grounds.
4. Heard the arguments of Sri. Gurudev Prasad.

K.T, learned counsel for the appellants and NC:
2023:KHC:38110 Sri. S. Krishna Kishore, learned counsel for the Insurance Company.

sentences.text: It is the contention of learned counsel for the petitioners that the deceased was working as an Office Assistant at Jain Biologicals Private Limited and earning Rs.15,100/- per month.

But the Tribunal has not considered the same and assessed notional income at Rs.6,000/- in determining the compensation and the Tribunal has awarded interest at 6% p.a. which is on the lower side and sought for enhancement with 12% interest.
6.

Per contra, learned counsel for the Insurance Company has contended that Ex.P12 is the certificate issued by Jain Biologicals Pvt. Ltd., it has no authenticity, there is no details about the salary paid and deduction affected towards professional tax and other statutory deduction, etc.
Even there is no material that the deceased has received salary from Jain Biologicals Pvt. Ltd.

If really the deceased was NC: 2023:KHC:38110 earning salary of Rs.10,000/- per month plus other allowances,
it ought to have paid to his bank account.

The Tribunal has rightly considered in the absence of proof of income, Ex.P12 cannot be relied upon and recorded that the deceased was a person with no proof of income and assessed the notional income at Rs.6,000/-.
At the time of accident, the prevailing bank rate of interest is lesser than 6% and there is no need for enhancement of compensation or rate of interest

and he supported the impugned judgment.
7. I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments addressed on both sides and also perused the materials on record.
8.
Before the Tribunal, this is second round of litigation.
Earlier when the claim was decided on 21.01.2013, compensation of Rs.11,28,000/- was awarded by taking the income of the deceased at Rs.9,000/- per month.
The said judgment and NC: 2023:KHC:38110 decree was set aside by virtue of the order passed in Misc.No.78/2014 by order dated 20.09.2014.
In the 2nd round, the Tribunal after taking the evidence, assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.6,000/- per month.
9. The dispute is only with regard to the income of the deceased.
Before the Tribunal, the evidence of PW-3 Sri. Shivakumar and Ex.P12 is relied to prove the employment and the income of the deceased.
I have perused the evidence of PW-3, Ex.P12 and the impugned judgment.
The Tribunal has discussed in-detail the evidence that the deceased was paid Rs.10,000/-, fuel allowance of Rs.150/- per day, telephone charges of Rs.600/- per month.
The cross-examination of PW-3 has demonstrated that the deceased was working as an Office Assistant, but his employment is only for 6 months.
He was under probationary period and he is not a permanent employee.
The petitioners have not NC: 2023:KHC:38110 produced any document to show that a sum of Rs.15,100/- was received by the deceased.
Jain Biologicals Pvt. Ltd. is a limited company and there is no scope for payment of salary by cash.

If the petitioners have produced the documents like bank statement,
salary slip, that could have been a different one, but the blank certificate is produced to show that the deceased has paid so much of salary, deductions towards professional tax and other deductions effected to an employee like provident fund or insurance.
There are no such deductions in Ex.P12.

Though the Tribunal has considered the deceased as a person with no proof of income, the income of Rs.6,000/- assessed is on the lower side having regard to his avocation and therefore, a sum of Rs.8,000/- could be the notional income that one can earn in the year 2010.

In a case of this nature, principles of assessment of compensation is settled by the NC:
2023:KHC:38110 Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Co.Ltd.
-vs- Pranay Sethi and Others1and Sarla Varma (Smt.) and Others -vs- Delhi Transport Corporation and Another2.

sentences.text: By applying these principles, compensation has to be assessed.
Since, the deceased was aged 46 years with no proof of income, future prospects of 30% has to be considered.
There are 4 dependents and therefore, 1/4th has to be deducted towards personal expenses.

If all these factors are reconsidered, the assessment of loss of dependency will be Rs.8,000/- + Rs.2,400/- (30%) =
Rs.10,400/- - Rs.2,600/- (1/4th) = Rs.7,800/- x 12 x '13' multiplier = Rs.12,16,800/-.
Under conventional heads, towards loss of consortium to wife, loss of love and affection to children and mother, a sum of Rs.20,000/- each has to be assessed.
Towards funeral expenses and (2017) 16 SCC 680 (2009) 6 SCC 121 NC: 2023:KHC:38110 loss of estate, Rs.10,000/- each has to be assessed.
If all these are summed up, it comes to Rs.13,16,800/- as against Rs.10,82,600/-, thereby enhancement of Rs.2,34,200/-.
This is the just compensation that the petitioners are entitled to, in the facts and circumstances of the case.
Hence, the appeal merits consideration, in the result, the following:
ORDER i) Appeal is allowed in part.
ii) Impugned judgment is modified.

iii) Petitioners are entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.2,34,200/- with interest of 6% p.a.
iv) The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the compensation within eight weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of the judgment.
- 10 - NC: 2023:KHC:38110 v) Amount in deposit, if any, shall be transmitted to the Tribunal along with records forthwith.
